His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: I know nothing except what Allah teaches me, and the knowledge of Allah, exalted be He, cannot be counted. I have only been commanded to convey to you that there is no god but Allah.

(﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: whoever hopes to see Him and to receive His reward, and fears His punishment.

(﴿let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110].

Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Jundub ibn Zuhayr al-'Amiri, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do an action for the sake of Allah, exalted be He, and I intend by it the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, except that when it is seen by others, it pleases me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and He does not accept what has been shared with another." Then the verse was revealed.

Tawus said: a man said, "O Messenger of Allah! I love to fight in the way of Allah, exalted be He, and I love that my position be seen," so this verse was revealed.

Mujahid said: a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah! I give charity and maintain the ties of kinship, and I do that only for Allah, exalted be He, but it is mentioned about me, and I am praised for it, and that pleases me and impresses me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent and said nothing, so Allah, exalted be He, revealed: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: all of these are meant, and the verse includes all of that and other deeds.

The sound hadith of Abu Hurairah about the three people who will be judged first among mankind has already been mentioned in Surah Hud[[See vol. 9, p. 14.]]. And the discussion of showing off (riya') has already been mentioned in Surah al-Nisa'[[See vol. 5, p. 180 onward.]], where we also mentioned from the reports there what is sufficient.

Al-Mawardi said, and all the people of interpretation said: the meaning of His saying, exalted be He: "and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110] is that he does not show off his deed to anyone.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in (Nawadir al-Usul): He said: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd told us, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, who said: I came to Shaddad ibn Aws at his place of prayer, and he was weeping. I said: "What made you weep, O Abu Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "A hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day. I saw on his face something that troubled me. I said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, what is it that I see on your face?' He said: 'A matter I fear for my community after me.' I said: 'What is it, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Shirk and hidden desire.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Will your community associate partners with Allah after you?' He said: 'O Shaddad! Indeed they will not worship the sun, nor the moon, nor a stone, nor an idol, but they will show off with their deeds.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is showing off shirk?" He said: "Yes." I said: "What is the hidden desire?" He said: "A person wakes up fasting, then the desires of this world are presented to him, and he breaks his fast." 

Abd al-Wahid said: I met al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id! Tell me about showing off: is it shirk?" He said: "Yes. Do you not recite: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord' [al-Kahf: 110]?"

Ismail ibn Ishaq narrated: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Shaddad ibn Aws were sitting together, and they said: "We fear for this community from shirk and hidden desire." As for hidden desire, it comes from women. They also said: "We heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever prays a prayer showing off with it has committed shirk, and whoever fasts a fast showing off with it has committed shirk.'" Then they recited: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: the interpretation of hidden desire has come differently from this, and we have mentioned it in (al-Nisa')[[See vol. 5, p. 181.]].

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: al-Hasan was asked about sincerity (ikhlas) and showing off (riya'), and he said: "From sincerity is that you love to conceal your good deeds and do not love to conceal your bad deeds. If Allah makes your good deeds apparent, you say: 'This is from Your grace and kindness, and it is not from my action or my doing.'" And he recalled the saying of Allah, exalted be He: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and ﴿those who give what they give﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 60] — the verse — who give sincerity while fearing that it will not be accepted from them. As for showing off, it is seeking the portion of the self from its deed in this world. It was said to him: "How is this?" He said: "Whoever seeks, by a deed between himself and Allah, exalted be He, other than the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, and the Hereafter, that is showing off."

Our scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, said: showing off may lead its doer to be mocked by people, as it is related that Tahir ibn al-Husayn said to Abu Abd Allah al-Marwazi: "How long has it been since you came to Iraq, O Abu Abd Allah?" He said: "I entered Iraq twenty years ago, and I have been fasting for thirty years." He said: "O Abu Abd Allah, we asked you one question and you answered us with two."

Al-Asma'i related that a Bedouin prayed and lengthened his prayer, and beside him were some people. They said: "How beautiful is your prayer!" He said: "And I am fasting along with that." Compare this with the saying of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, who prayed and shortened it. It was said to him: "You have shortened it," and he said: "Indeed, it was not mixed with showing off," so he was free of their belittling by negating showing off from himself, and from the affectation in his prayer. The remedy for showing off has already been mentioned in al-Nisa', from the saying of Luqman, that it is the concealment of the deed.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: al-Himmani informed us, saying: Jarir informed us, from Layth, from a shaykh, from [[In manuscript K: he said.]] Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Bakr said, and he testified to it upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned shirk, and he said: "It is among you more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Shall I direct you to something which, if you do it, removes from you the minor and major shirk? Say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know,' say it three times." 

Umar ibn Qays al-Kindi said: I heard Mu'awiyah recite this verse on the pulpit: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and he said: "Indeed, it is the last verse to be revealed from the heaven."

Umar said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "It has been revealed to me that whoever recites 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds' [al-Kahf: 110], a light will be raised for him between Aden and Makkah, filled with angels who send blessings upon him and seek forgiveness for him."

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever recites the beginning of Surah al-Kahf and its end, it will be a light for him from his head to his feet, and whoever recites all of it, it will be a light for him from the earth to the sky."

It is related from Ibn Abbas that a man said to him: "I intend to get up for a while in the night, but sleep overcomes me." He said: "When you want to get up at any hour of the night you wish, recite, when you lie down on your bed: 'Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord' [al-Kahf: 109] to the end of the surah, for Allah, exalted be He, will wake you at whatever hour of the night you wish." Al-Tha'labi, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned these virtues.

In the Musnad of al-Darimi, Abu Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, from al-Awza'i, from Abdah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: "Whoever recites the end of Surah al-Kahf for an hour he wishes to get up in the night, he will get up at that hour." Abdah said: "We tested it and found it to be so."

Ibn al-Arabi said: Our shaykh al-Turtushi the Elder used to say: "Let not the times lead you astray into contending with peers and maintaining ties with brothers." Allah, glorified and exalted be He, concluded the exposition with His saying: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 18, verses 99–110 (part 1 of 2)**

Allah's words: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging against one another.﴾ The pronoun in "We will leave" refers to Allah, meaning: We will leave the jinn and mankind on the Day of Resurrection surging, some of them against others. It was also said: "We will leave Ya'juj and Ma'juj on that day," meaning at the time when the barrier is complete, surging, some of them against others. The metaphor of surging (mawj) for them expresses bewilderment and the milling of some of them among others, like those distracted by grief and fear. He likened them to the surging of the sea, whose waves churn one against another. It was also said: "We will leave Ya'juj and Ma'juj on the day the barrier is breached, surging in the world, mixed together because of their great numbers." I say: These are three opinions. The most apparent of them is the middle one, and the furthest is the last. The first is good, because the Resurrection was mentioned earlier in the interpretation of His words: ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes.﴾ And Allah knows best.

Allah's words: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown.﴾ This has been discussed in (al-An'am) [[See vol. 7, p. 20 ff.]].

(Then We will gather them in a gathering) meaning the jinn and mankind in the open plains of the Resurrection.

(And We will present Hell) 100, meaning We will make it manifest to them.

(On that day, to the disbelievers, in full display) 100. (Those whose eyes were) is in the genitive position as a qualifier of "the disbelievers."

(Under a covering from My remembrance) 101, meaning: they are in the position of one whose eye is covered, so he does not look at the signs of Allah.

(And they could not hear) 101, meaning: they could not bear to hear the speech of Allah, so they are in the position of one who is deaf.

Allah's words: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think﴾ 102, meaning: suppose. Ali, Ikrimah, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin read "afahasiba" with the sin sukun and the ba' with damma, meaning: it suffices them.

(That they may take My servants) 102, meaning Jesus, the angels and Uzayr,

(as protectors instead of Me) 102. And I will not punish them. So there is an ellipsis in the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: have they supposed that this will benefit them?

(Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging) 102.

Allah's words: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ 102 up to His words (weight), there are two issues.

The first: His words ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ 102, and the verse as a whole, indicate that among people is one who does a deed while thinking he is doing good, and his effort has been nullified. What causes the nullification of effort is either corruption of belief or showing off, and what is meant here is disbelief. Al-Bukhari narrated from Mus'ab who said: I asked my father about "Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? 102" – are they the Harurites? He said: No, they are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad (ﷺ), and as for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise, saying: there is no food in it and no drink. The Harurites are those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation, and Sa'd used to call them the wicked. The verse means reproach: say to these disbelievers who worship other than Me: their effort and hopes will be disappointed tomorrow, so they are the greatest losers in deeds, and they are ﴿those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work﴾ 104 – in worshipping other than Me. Ibn Abbas said: he means the disbelievers of the people of Makkah. Ali said: they are the Kharijites, the people of Harura'. Murrah said: they are the monks, the people of the cloisters. It is narrated that Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about "the greatest losers in deeds," and he said to him: you and your companions. Ibn Atiyya said: all of this is weakened by His words after that: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and His meeting, so their deeds have become void﴾ 105. None of these groups denies Allah, His meeting, the Resurrection and the Gathering, and this is the description of the idolatrous Makkans, the worshippers of idols. Ali and Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with them both, mentioned groups who took their share of this verse [[In (j) : the Arabs.]] [[In (k) and (ā): from the beginning of the verse.]]. "Deeds" (a'malan) is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz). The reading of the majority for "habitat" (habitat) is with the kasra on the ba'. Ibn Abbas read "habatat" with the fatha.

The second: His words ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ 105. The reading of the majority is "nuqim" with the plural of majesty (the "we" form). Mujahid read it with the yā' of the third-person absent, meaning: Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, will not establish. Ubayd ibn Umayr read "fala yaqum" (it will not stand), which requires that he read "wazn" (weight) in the nominative. Mujahid similarly read: "So there will not stand for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight." Ubayd ibn Umayr said: On the Day of Resurrection a man, great, tall and a great eater and drinker, will be brought, and he will not weigh with Allah the wing of a gnat. I say: This cannot be said by opinion alone, and its meaning has been established as a report traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, a great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh with Allah the wing of a gnat." Recite if you wish: ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The meaning is that they have no reward, and their deeds are met with punishment, so there is no good deed for them to be weighed on the scales of the Resurrection, and whoever has no good deed is in the Fire. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: Deeds like the mountains of Tihama will be brought, and they will not weigh anything. It was also said: it may mean metaphor and figurative speech, as if He said: "So there will be no value for them with Us on that day," and Allah knows best. In this hadith there is jurisprudence (fiqh) disparaging fatness for one who strives to acquire it, because in that there is the pursuit of foods and occupation with them away from noble qualities. Rather, it indicates the prohibition of eating beyond the amount needed for sustenance, sought for luxury and fattening. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the most hateful of men to Allah, may He be exalted, is the fat scholar (habr)." And from the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The best of you is my generation, then those who follow them" – Imran said: I do not know whether he mentioned two generations after his generation or three – "then after you there will be a people who bear witness without being asked, who betray and are not trusted, who make vows and do not fulfil them, and fatness appears among them." (This is a condemnation.) The reason for this is that acquired fatness comes only from excessive eating and greed, and from ease, comfort, safety and indulgence with the self in its desires. Such a person is a slave to his self, not a slave to his Lord, and whoever is in this state inevitably falls into what is forbidden, and every flesh that grows from unlawful gain, the Fire is more fitting for it. Allah, may He be exalted, has condemned the disbelievers for their excessive eating, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ [[See vol. 16, p. 234.]] [Muhammad: 12]. So if the believer resembles them and enjoys their luxury in all his states and times, where is the reality of faith, and the performance of the duties of Islam?! Whoever eats and drinks much, his greed and eagerness increase, and his laziness and sleep increase at night, so his day is lost and his night is asleep. This meaning has passed in (al-A'raf) [[See vol. 7, p. 191 ff. and p. 165.]], and the mention of the Scale has preceded there, and that it has two pans in which the records of deeds are weighed, so there is no point in repeating it. And when they laughed at the thinness of the shin (hamsh) [[Hamsh al-saq: its thinness.]] of Ibn Mas'ud while he was climbing a palm tree, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Do you laugh at a shin that will be weighed with the deeds of the people of the earth?" This indicates that persons are weighed. This was mentioned by al-Ghaznawi.

Allah's words: ﴿That is their recompense﴾. "That" refers to the abandonment of weighing, and it is in the nominative position as a subject. "Their recompense" is its predicate, and (Hell) 106 is an apposition to the subject which is "that." The "ma" in His words "because they disbelieved" 106 is verbal (masdariyya), and "mockery" (huzu') means belittling and derision, which has been discussed.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging﴾ 107. Qatadah said: al-Firdaws is the hill of Paradise, its middle, its highest, its best and its loftiest. Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: al-Firdaws is the navel of Paradise. Ka'b said: There is no garden among the gardens higher than the Garden of al-Firdaws; in it are those who enjoin the good and forbid the evil. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes the prayer and fasts Ramadan, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise, whether he struggles in the way of Allah or sits in his land in which he was born." They said: O Messenger of Allah, should we not inform the people with glad tidings? He said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees which Allah has prepared for those who struggle in the way of Allah; between each two degrees is as between the heaven and the earth. So when you ask Allah, the Exalted, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest of Paradise – I think he said – and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth." Mujahid said: al-Firdaws is the orchard in Byzantine (Rumi) language. Al-Farra' said: it is Arabic. Al-Firdaws is a garden in Paradise. Firdaws is also the name of a meadow below al-Yamamah. Its plural is faradis. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi said:

"Their dwellings were then evident, in them the faradis, the garlic (fuwman) and the onion."

Al-Faradis is a place in Syria. And a "mufradas" vine means trellised (mu'arrash).

(Abiding therein) meaning: remaining forever.

(They will not desire to be removed from it) 108, meaning they will not seek a transfer from it to anything else. "Hiwal" means transfer (tahwil). Abu Ali said this. Al-Zajjaj said: he removed from his place "hiwalan" just as one says "he grew great in greatness" (ʿazuma ʿiẓaman). He said: It may also be from "hila" (trickery), meaning they will not seek a dwelling other than it. Al-Jawhari said: "Tahawwul" is movement from one place to another, and the noun is "hiwal," and from it is the saying of Allah: ﴿Abiding therein, they will not desire to be removed from it﴾ 108.

Allah's words: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾ 109. "Nafida" means a thing is complete and finished, and this has been discussed before.

(And even if We brought the like of it as replenishment) 109, meaning: an addition to the sea in number or weight. In the codex of Ubayy it is "midadan" 109, and so Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin and Humayd read it. "Madadan" 109 is in the accusative as a specification or as a circumstantial state (hal). Ibn Abbas said: The Jews said when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [[See vol. 10, p. 323.]] [al-Isra': 85], they said: How, when we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good? So this was revealed: "Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted" 109, to the end of the verse. It was also said: The Jews said: You have been given wisdom, and whoever has been given wisdom has been given much good; then you claim you have no knowledge of the Spirit?! So Allah, the Exalted, said: Say: even if you were given the Qur'an and you were given the Torah, it is, in relation to the words of Allah, little. Ibn Abbas said: "The words of my Lord" 109 means: the admonitions of my Lord. It was also said: By "the words" he means the eternal speech which has no limit and no end, and though it is one, it is permissible to express it with the plural form, because it contains wondrous words, and because it is a means for us through them. So the expression in plural form is permitted, for majesty. Al-A'sha said:

"And a face clear in colour, pure, adorned by it, with a neck, and with the lobes and the wrists."

The Arabic says "فَعَبَّرَ بِاللَّبَّاتِ عَنِ اللَّبَّةِ", which means he used the plural *al-labbat* to refer to the singular *al-labbah*. In the Revelation: ﴿We are your allies﴾ [Fussilat: 31][[See vol. 15, p. 357.]]. And ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder﴾ [al-Hijr: 9][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]]. And ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾ [al-Hijr: 23][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]]. Likewise ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾ [al-Nahl: 120][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]], because he took the place of a nation.

It was also said: meaning, the expressions and indications that point to the understood meanings of the words of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, would not be exhausted.

Al-Suddi said: meaning, even if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the attributes of Paradise, which is the abode of reward, were exhausted.

Ikrimah said: the sea would be exhausted before the reward of the one who says "There is no god but Allah" is exhausted.

A parallel to this verse is: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman: 27][[See vol. 13, p. 76.]].

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْفَدَ" with the *ya'* (in the third person masculine), because the verb had already been mentioned.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: I know nothing except what Allah teaches me, and the knowledge of Allah, exalted be He, cannot be counted. I have only been commanded to convey to you that there is no god but Allah.

(﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: whoever hopes to see Him and to receive His reward, and fears His punishment.

(﴿let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110].

Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Jundub ibn Zuhayr al-'Amiri, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do an action for the sake of Allah, exalted be He, and I intend by it the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, except that when it is seen by others, it pleases me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and He does not accept what has been shared with another." Then the verse was revealed.

Tawus said: a man said, "O Messenger of Allah! I love to fight in the way of Allah, exalted be He, and I love that my position be seen," so this verse was revealed.

Mujahid said: a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah! I give charity and maintain the ties of kinship, and I do that only for Allah, exalted be He, but it is mentioned about me, and I am praised for it, and that pleases me and impresses me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent and said nothing, so Allah, exalted be He, revealed: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: all of these are meant, and the verse includes all of that and other deeds.

The sound hadith of Abu Hurairah about the three people who will be judged first among mankind has already been mentioned in Surah Hud[[See vol. 9, p. 14.]]. And the discussion of showing off (riya') has already been mentioned in Surah al-Nisa'[[See vol. 5, p. 180 onward.]], where we also mentioned from the reports there what is sufficient.

Al-Mawardi said, and all the people of interpretation said: the meaning of His saying, exalted be He: "and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110] is that he does not show off his deed to anyone.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in (Nawadir al-Usul): He said: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd told us, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, who said: I came to Shaddad ibn Aws at his place of prayer, and he was weeping. I said: "What made you weep, O Abu Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "A hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day. I saw on his face something that troubled me. I said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, what is it that I see on your face?' He said: 'A matter I fear for my community after me.' I said: 'What is it, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Shirk and hidden desire.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Will your community associate partners with Allah after you?' He said: 'O Shaddad! Indeed they will not worship the sun, nor the moon, nor a stone, nor an idol, but they will show off with their deeds.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is showing off shirk?" He said: "Yes." I said: "What is the hidden desire?" He said: "A person wakes up fasting, then the desires of this world are presented to him, and he breaks his fast." 

Abd al-Wahid said: I met al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id! Tell me about showing off: is it shirk?" He said: "Yes. Do you not recite: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord' [al-Kahf: 110]?"

Ismail ibn Ishaq narrated: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Shaddad ibn Aws were sitting together, and they said: "We fear for this community from shirk and hidden desire." As for hidden desire, it comes from women. They also said: "We heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever prays a prayer showing off with it has committed shirk, and whoever fasts a fast showing off with it has committed shirk.'" Then they recited: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: the interpretation of hidden desire has come differently from this, and we have mentioned it in (al-Nisa')[[See vol. 5, p. 181.]].

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: al-Hasan was asked about sincerity (ikhlas) and showing off (riya'), and he said: "From sincerity is that you love to conceal your good deeds and do not love to conceal your bad deeds. If Allah makes your good deeds apparent, you say: 'This is from Your grace and kindness, and it is not from my action or my doing.'" And he recalled the saying of Allah, exalted be He: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and ﴿those who give what they give﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 60] — the verse — who give sincerity while fearing that it will not be accepted from them. As for showing off, it is seeking the portion of the self from its deed in this world. It was said to him: "How is this?" He said: "Whoever seeks, by a deed between himself and Allah, exalted be He, other than the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, and the Hereafter, that is showing off."

Our scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, said: showing off may lead its doer to be mocked by people, as it is related that Tahir ibn al-Husayn said to Abu Abd Allah al-Marwazi: "How long has it been since you came to Iraq, O Abu Abd Allah?" He said: "I entered Iraq twenty years ago, and I have been fasting for thirty years." He said: "O Abu Abd Allah, we asked you one question and you answered us with two."

Al-Asma'i related that a Bedouin prayed and lengthened his prayer, and beside him were some people. They said: "How beautiful is your prayer!" He said: "And I am fasting along with that." Compare this with the saying of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, who prayed and shortened it. It was said to him: "You have shortened it," and he said: "Indeed, it was not mixed with showing off," so he was free of their belittling by negating showing off from himself, and from the affectation in his prayer. The remedy for showing off has already been mentioned in al-Nisa', from the saying of Luqman, that it is the concealment of the deed.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: al-Himmani informed us, saying: Jarir informed us, from Layth, from a shaykh, from [[In manuscript K: he said.]] Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Bakr said, and he testified to it upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned shirk, and he said: "It is among you more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Shall I direct you to something which, if you do it, removes from you the minor and major shirk? Say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know,' say it three times." 

Umar ibn Qays al-Kindi said: I heard Mu'awiyah recite this verse on the pulpit: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and he said: "Indeed, it is the last verse to be revealed from the heaven."

Umar said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "It has been revealed to me that whoever recites 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds' [al-Kahf: 110], a light will be raised for him between Aden and Makkah, filled with angels who send blessings upon him and seek forgiveness for him."

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever recites the beginning of Surah al-Kahf and its end, it will be a light for him from his head to his feet, and whoever recites all of it, it will be a light for him from the earth to the sky."

It is related from Ibn Abbas that a man said to him: "I intend to get up for a while in the night, but sleep overcomes me." He said: "When you want to get up at any hour of the night you wish, recite, when you lie down on your bed: 'Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord' [al-Kahf: 109] to the end of the surah, for Allah, exalted be He, will wake you at whatever hour of the night you wish." Al-Tha'labi, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned these virtues.

In the Musnad of al-Darimi, Abu Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, from al-Awza'i, from Abdah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: "Whoever recites the end of Surah al-Kahf for an hour he wishes to get up in the night, he will get up at that hour." Abdah said: "We tested it and found it to be so."

Ibn al-Arabi said: Our shaykh al-Turtushi the Elder used to say: "Let not the times lead you astray into contending with peers and maintaining ties with brothers." Allah, glorified and exalted be He, concluded the exposition with His saying: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 18, verses 99–110 (part 1 of 2)**

Allah's words: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging against one another.﴾ The pronoun in "We will leave" refers to Allah, meaning: We will leave the jinn and mankind on the Day of Resurrection surging, some of them against others. It was also said: "We will leave Ya'juj and Ma'juj on that day," meaning at the time when the barrier is complete, surging, some of them against others. The metaphor of surging (mawj) for them expresses bewilderment and the milling of some of them among others, like those distracted by grief and fear. He likened them to the surging of the sea, whose waves churn one against another. It was also said: "We will leave Ya'juj and Ma'juj on the day the barrier is breached, surging in the world, mixed together because of their great numbers." I say: These are three opinions. The most apparent of them is the middle one, and the furthest is the last. The first is good, because the Resurrection was mentioned earlier in the interpretation of His words: ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes.﴾ And Allah knows best.

Allah's words: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown.﴾ This has been discussed in (al-An'am) [[See vol. 7, p. 20 ff.]].

(Then We will gather them in a gathering) meaning the jinn and mankind in the open plains of the Resurrection.

(And We will present Hell) 100, meaning We will make it manifest to them.

(On that day, to the disbelievers, in full display) 100. (Those whose eyes were) is in the genitive position as a qualifier of "the disbelievers."

(Under a covering from My remembrance) 101, meaning: they are in the position of one whose eye is covered, so he does not look at the signs of Allah.

(And they could not hear) 101, meaning: they could not bear to hear the speech of Allah, so they are in the position of one who is deaf.

Allah's words: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think﴾ 102, meaning: suppose. Ali, Ikrimah, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin read "afahasiba" with the sin sukun and the ba' with damma, meaning: it suffices them.

(That they may take My servants) 102, meaning Jesus, the angels and Uzayr,

(as protectors instead of Me) 102. And I will not punish them. So there is an ellipsis in the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: have they supposed that this will benefit them?

(Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging) 102.

Allah's words: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ 102 up to His words (weight), there are two issues.

The first: His words ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ 102, and the verse as a whole, indicate that among people is one who does a deed while thinking he is doing good, and his effort has been nullified. What causes the nullification of effort is either corruption of belief or showing off, and what is meant here is disbelief. Al-Bukhari narrated from Mus'ab who said: I asked my father about "Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? 102" – are they the Harurites? He said: No, they are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad (ﷺ), and as for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise, saying: there is no food in it and no drink. The Harurites are those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation, and Sa'd used to call them the wicked. The verse means reproach: say to these disbelievers who worship other than Me: their effort and hopes will be disappointed tomorrow, so they are the greatest losers in deeds, and they are ﴿those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work﴾ 104 – in worshipping other than Me. Ibn Abbas said: he means the disbelievers of the people of Makkah. Ali said: they are the Kharijites, the people of Harura'. Murrah said: they are the monks, the people of the cloisters. It is narrated that Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about "the greatest losers in deeds," and he said to him: you and your companions. Ibn Atiyya said: all of this is weakened by His words after that: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and His meeting, so their deeds have become void﴾ 105. None of these groups denies Allah, His meeting, the Resurrection and the Gathering, and this is the description of the idolatrous Makkans, the worshippers of idols. Ali and Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with them both, mentioned groups who took their share of this verse [[In (j) : the Arabs.]] [[In (k) and (ā): from the beginning of the verse.]]. "Deeds" (a'malan) is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz). The reading of the majority for "habitat" (habitat) is with the kasra on the ba'. Ibn Abbas read "habatat" with the fatha.

The second: His words ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ 105. The reading of the majority is "nuqim" with the plural of majesty (the "we" form). Mujahid read it with the yā' of the third-person absent, meaning: Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, will not establish. Ubayd ibn Umayr read "fala yaqum" (it will not stand), which requires that he read "wazn" (weight) in the nominative. Mujahid similarly read: "So there will not stand for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight." Ubayd ibn Umayr said: On the Day of Resurrection a man, great, tall and a great eater and drinker, will be brought, and he will not weigh with Allah the wing of a gnat. I say: This cannot be said by opinion alone, and its meaning has been established as a report traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, a great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh with Allah the wing of a gnat." Recite if you wish: ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The meaning is that they have no reward, and their deeds are met with punishment, so there is no good deed for them to be weighed on the scales of the Resurrection, and whoever has no good deed is in the Fire. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: Deeds like the mountains of Tihama will be brought, and they will not weigh anything. It was also said: it may mean metaphor and figurative speech, as if He said: "So there will be no value for them with Us on that day," and Allah knows best. In this hadith there is jurisprudence (fiqh) disparaging fatness for one who strives to acquire it, because in that there is the pursuit of foods and occupation with them away from noble qualities. Rather, it indicates the prohibition of eating beyond the amount needed for sustenance, sought for luxury and fattening. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the most hateful of men to Allah, may He be exalted, is the fat scholar (habr)." And from the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The best of you is my generation, then those who follow them" – Imran said: I do not know whether he mentioned two generations after his generation or three – "then after you there will be a people who bear witness without being asked, who betray and are not trusted, who make vows and do not fulfil them, and fatness appears among them." (This is a condemnation.) The reason for this is that acquired fatness comes only from excessive eating and greed, and from ease, comfort, safety and indulgence with the self in its desires. Such a person is a slave to his self, not a slave to his Lord, and whoever is in this state inevitably falls into what is forbidden, and every flesh that grows from unlawful gain, the Fire is more fitting for it. Allah, may He be exalted, has condemned the disbelievers for their excessive eating, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ [[See vol. 16, p. 234.]] [Muhammad: 12]. So if the believer resembles them and enjoys their luxury in all his states and times, where is the reality of faith, and the performance of the duties of Islam?! Whoever eats and drinks much, his greed and eagerness increase, and his laziness and sleep increase at night, so his day is lost and his night is asleep. This meaning has passed in (al-A'raf) [[See vol. 7, p. 191 ff. and p. 165.]], and the mention of the Scale has preceded there, and that it has two pans in which the records of deeds are weighed, so there is no point in repeating it. And when they laughed at the thinness of the shin (hamsh) [[Hamsh al-saq: its thinness.]] of Ibn Mas'ud while he was climbing a palm tree, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Do you laugh at a shin that will be weighed with the deeds of the people of the earth?" This indicates that persons are weighed. This was mentioned by al-Ghaznawi.

Allah's words: ﴿That is their recompense﴾. "That" refers to the abandonment of weighing, and it is in the nominative position as a subject. "Their recompense" is its predicate, and (Hell) 106 is an apposition to the subject which is "that." The "ma" in His words "because they disbelieved" 106 is verbal (masdariyya), and "mockery" (huzu') means belittling and derision, which has been discussed.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging﴾ 107. Qatadah said: al-Firdaws is the hill of Paradise, its middle, its highest, its best and its loftiest. Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: al-Firdaws is the navel of Paradise. Ka'b said: There is no garden among the gardens higher than the Garden of al-Firdaws; in it are those who enjoin the good and forbid the evil. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes the prayer and fasts Ramadan, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise, whether he struggles in the way of Allah or sits in his land in which he was born." They said: O Messenger of Allah, should we not inform the people with glad tidings? He said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees which Allah has prepared for those who struggle in the way of Allah; between each two degrees is as between the heaven and the earth. So when you ask Allah, the Exalted, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest of Paradise – I think he said – and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth." Mujahid said: al-Firdaws is the orchard in Byzantine (Rumi) language. Al-Farra' said: it is Arabic. Al-Firdaws is a garden in Paradise. Firdaws is also the name of a meadow below al-Yamamah. Its plural is faradis. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi said:

"Their dwellings were then evident, in them the faradis, the garlic (fuwman) and the onion."

Al-Faradis is a place in Syria. And a "mufradas" vine means trellised (mu'arrash).

(Abiding therein) meaning: remaining forever.

(They will not desire to be removed from it) 108, meaning they will not seek a transfer from it to anything else. "Hiwal" means transfer (tahwil). Abu Ali said this. Al-Zajjaj said: he removed from his place "hiwalan" just as one says "he grew great in greatness" (ʿazuma ʿiẓaman). He said: It may also be from "hila" (trickery), meaning they will not seek a dwelling other than it. Al-Jawhari said: "Tahawwul" is movement from one place to another, and the noun is "hiwal," and from it is the saying of Allah: ﴿Abiding therein, they will not desire to be removed from it﴾ 108.

Allah's words: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾ 109. "Nafida" means a thing is complete and finished, and this has been discussed before.

(And even if We brought the like of it as replenishment) 109, meaning: an addition to the sea in number or weight. In the codex of Ubayy it is "midadan" 109, and so Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin and Humayd read it. "Madadan" 109 is in the accusative as a specification or as a circumstantial state (hal). Ibn Abbas said: The Jews said when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [[See vol. 10, p. 323.]] [al-Isra': 85], they said: How, when we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good? So this was revealed: "Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted" 109, to the end of the verse. It was also said: The Jews said: You have been given wisdom, and whoever has been given wisdom has been given much good; then you claim you have no knowledge of the Spirit?! So Allah, the Exalted, said: Say: even if you were given the Qur'an and you were given the Torah, it is, in relation to the words of Allah, little. Ibn Abbas said: "The words of my Lord" 109 means: the admonitions of my Lord. It was also said: By "the words" he means the eternal speech which has no limit and no end, and though it is one, it is permissible to express it with the plural form, because it contains wondrous words, and because it is a means for us through them. So the expression in plural form is permitted, for majesty. Al-A'sha said:

"And a face clear in colour, pure, adorned by it, with a neck, and with the lobes and the wrists."

The Arabic says "فَعَبَّرَ بِاللَّبَّاتِ عَنِ اللَّبَّةِ", which means he used the plural *al-labbat* to refer to the singular *al-labbah*. In the Revelation: ﴿We are your allies﴾ [Fussilat: 31][[See vol. 15, p. 357.]]. And ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder﴾ [al-Hijr: 9][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]]. And ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾ [al-Hijr: 23][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]]. Likewise ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾ [al-Nahl: 120][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]], because he took the place of a nation.

It was also said: meaning, the expressions and indications that point to the understood meanings of the words of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, would not be exhausted.

Al-Suddi said: meaning, even if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the attributes of Paradise, which is the abode of reward, were exhausted.

Ikrimah said: the sea would be exhausted before the reward of the one who says "There is no god but Allah" is exhausted.

A parallel to this verse is: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman: 27][[See vol. 13, p. 76.]].

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْفَدَ" with the *ya'* (in the third person masculine), because the verb had already been mentioned.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: I know nothing except what Allah teaches me, and the knowledge of Allah, exalted be He, cannot be counted. I have only been commanded to convey to you that there is no god but Allah.

(﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: whoever hopes to see Him and to receive His reward, and fears His punishment.

(﴿let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110].

Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Jundub ibn Zuhayr al-'Amiri, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do an action for the sake of Allah, exalted be He, and I intend by it the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, except that when it is seen by others, it pleases me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and He does not accept what has been shared with another." Then the verse was revealed.

Tawus said: a man said, "O Messenger of Allah! I love to fight in the way of Allah, exalted be He, and I love that my position be seen," so this verse was revealed.

Mujahid said: a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah! I give charity and maintain the ties of kinship, and I do that only for Allah, exalted be He, but it is mentioned about me, and I am praised for it, and that pleases me and impresses me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent and said nothing, so Allah, exalted be He, revealed: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: all of these are meant, and the verse includes all of that and other deeds.

The sound hadith of Abu Hurairah about the three people who will be judged first among mankind has already been mentioned in Surah Hud[[See vol. 9, p. 14.]]. And the discussion of showing off (riya') has already been mentioned in Surah al-Nisa'[[See vol. 5, p. 180 onward.]], where we also mentioned from the reports there what is sufficient.

Al-Mawardi said, and all the people of interpretation said: the meaning of His saying, exalted be He: "and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110] is that he does not show off his deed to anyone.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in (Nawadir al-Usul): He said: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd told us, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, who said: I came to Shaddad ibn Aws at his place of prayer, and he was weeping. I said: "What made you weep, O Abu Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "A hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day. I saw on his face something that troubled me. I said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, what is it that I see on your face?' He said: 'A matter I fear for my community after me.' I said: 'What is it, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Shirk and hidden desire.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Will your community associate partners with Allah after you?' He said: 'O Shaddad! Indeed they will not worship the sun, nor the moon, nor a stone, nor an idol, but they will show off with their deeds.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is showing off shirk?" He said: "Yes." I said: "What is the hidden desire?" He said: "A person wakes up fasting, then the desires of this world are presented to him, and he breaks his fast." 

Abd al-Wahid said: I met al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id! Tell me about showing off: is it shirk?" He said: "Yes. Do you not recite: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord' [al-Kahf: 110]?"

Ismail ibn Ishaq narrated: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Shaddad ibn Aws were sitting together, and they said: "We fear for this community from shirk and hidden desire." As for hidden desire, it comes from women. They also said: "We heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever prays a prayer showing off with it has committed shirk, and whoever fasts a fast showing off with it has committed shirk.'" Then they recited: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: the interpretation of hidden desire has come differently from this, and we have mentioned it in (al-Nisa')[[See vol. 5, p. 181.]].

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: al-Hasan was asked about sincerity (ikhlas) and showing off (riya'), and he said: "From sincerity is that you love to conceal your good deeds and do not love to conceal your bad deeds. If Allah makes your good deeds apparent, you say: 'This is from Your grace and kindness, and it is not from my action or my doing.'" And he recalled the saying of Allah, exalted be He: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and ﴿those who give what they give﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 60] — the verse — who give sincerity while fearing that it will not be accepted from them. As for showing off, it is seeking the portion of the self from its deed in this world. It was said to him: "How is this?" He said: "Whoever seeks, by a deed between himself and Allah, exalted be He, other than the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, and the Hereafter, that is showing off."

Our scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, said: showing off may lead its doer to be mocked by people, as it is related that Tahir ibn al-Husayn said to Abu Abd Allah al-Marwazi: "How long has it been since you came to Iraq, O Abu Abd Allah?" He said: "I entered Iraq twenty years ago, and I have been fasting for thirty years." He said: "O Abu Abd Allah, we asked you one question and you answered us with two."

Al-Asma'i related that a Bedouin prayed and lengthened his prayer, and beside him were some people. They said: "How beautiful is your prayer!" He said: "And I am fasting along with that." Compare this with the saying of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, who prayed and shortened it. It was said to him: "You have shortened it," and he said: "Indeed, it was not mixed with showing off," so he was free of their belittling by negating showing off from himself, and from the affectation in his prayer. The remedy for showing off has already been mentioned in al-Nisa', from the saying of Luqman, that it is the concealment of the deed.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: al-Himmani informed us, saying: Jarir informed us, from Layth, from a shaykh, from [[In manuscript K: he said.]] Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Bakr said, and he testified to it upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned shirk, and he said: "It is among you more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Shall I direct you to something which, if you do it, removes from you the minor and major shirk? Say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know,' say it three times." 

Umar ibn Qays al-Kindi said: I heard Mu'awiyah recite this verse on the pulpit: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and he said: "Indeed, it is the last verse to be revealed from the heaven."

Umar said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "It has been revealed to me that whoever recites 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds' [al-Kahf: 110], a light will be raised for him between Aden and Makkah, filled with angels who send blessings upon him and seek forgiveness for him."

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever recites the beginning of Surah al-Kahf and its end, it will be a light for him from his head to his feet, and whoever recites all of it, it will be a light for him from the earth to the sky."

It is related from Ibn Abbas that a man said to him: "I intend to get up for a while in the night, but sleep overcomes me." He said: "When you want to get up at any hour of the night you wish, recite, when you lie down on your bed: 'Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord' [al-Kahf: 109] to the end of the surah, for Allah, exalted be He, will wake you at whatever hour of the night you wish." Al-Tha'labi, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned these virtues.

In the Musnad of al-Darimi, Abu Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, from al-Awza'i, from Abdah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: "Whoever recites the end of Surah al-Kahf for an hour he wishes to get up in the night, he will get up at that hour." Abdah said: "We tested it and found it to be so."

Ibn al-Arabi said: Our shaykh al-Turtushi the Elder used to say: "Let not the times lead you astray into contending with peers and maintaining ties with brothers." Allah, glorified and exalted be He, concluded the exposition with His saying: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 18, verses 99–110 (part 1 of 2)**

Allah's words: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging against one another.﴾ The pronoun in "We will leave" refers to Allah, meaning: We will leave the jinn and mankind on the Day of Resurrection surging, some of them against others. It was also said: "We will leave Ya'juj and Ma'juj on that day," meaning at the time when the barrier is complete, surging, some of them against others. The metaphor of surging (mawj) for them expresses bewilderment and the milling of some of them among others, like those distracted by grief and fear. He likened them to the surging of the sea, whose waves churn one against another. It was also said: "We will leave Ya'juj and Ma'juj on the day the barrier is breached, surging in the world, mixed together because of their great numbers." I say: These are three opinions. The most apparent of them is the middle one, and the furthest is the last. The first is good, because the Resurrection was mentioned earlier in the interpretation of His words: ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes.﴾ And Allah knows best.

Allah's words: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown.﴾ This has been discussed in (al-An'am) [[See vol. 7, p. 20 ff.]].

(Then We will gather them in a gathering) meaning the jinn and mankind in the open plains of the Resurrection.

(And We will present Hell) 100, meaning We will make it manifest to them.

(On that day, to the disbelievers, in full display) 100. (Those whose eyes were) is in the genitive position as a qualifier of "the disbelievers."

(Under a covering from My remembrance) 101, meaning: they are in the position of one whose eye is covered, so he does not look at the signs of Allah.

(And they could not hear) 101, meaning: they could not bear to hear the speech of Allah, so they are in the position of one who is deaf.

Allah's words: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think﴾ 102, meaning: suppose. Ali, Ikrimah, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin read "afahasiba" with the sin sukun and the ba' with damma, meaning: it suffices them.

(That they may take My servants) 102, meaning Jesus, the angels and Uzayr,

(as protectors instead of Me) 102. And I will not punish them. So there is an ellipsis in the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: have they supposed that this will benefit them?

(Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging) 102.

Allah's words: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ 102 up to His words (weight), there are two issues.

The first: His words ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ 102, and the verse as a whole, indicate that among people is one who does a deed while thinking he is doing good, and his effort has been nullified. What causes the nullification of effort is either corruption of belief or showing off, and what is meant here is disbelief. Al-Bukhari narrated from Mus'ab who said: I asked my father about "Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? 102" – are they the Harurites? He said: No, they are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad (ﷺ), and as for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise, saying: there is no food in it and no drink. The Harurites are those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation, and Sa'd used to call them the wicked. The verse means reproach: say to these disbelievers who worship other than Me: their effort and hopes will be disappointed tomorrow, so they are the greatest losers in deeds, and they are ﴿those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work﴾ 104 – in worshipping other than Me. Ibn Abbas said: he means the disbelievers of the people of Makkah. Ali said: they are the Kharijites, the people of Harura'. Murrah said: they are the monks, the people of the cloisters. It is narrated that Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about "the greatest losers in deeds," and he said to him: you and your companions. Ibn Atiyya said: all of this is weakened by His words after that: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and His meeting, so their deeds have become void﴾ 105. None of these groups denies Allah, His meeting, the Resurrection and the Gathering, and this is the description of the idolatrous Makkans, the worshippers of idols. Ali and Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with them both, mentioned groups who took their share of this verse [[In (j) : the Arabs.]] [[In (k) and (ā): from the beginning of the verse.]]. "Deeds" (a'malan) is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz). The reading of the majority for "habitat" (habitat) is with the kasra on the ba'. Ibn Abbas read "habatat" with the fatha.

The second: His words ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ 105. The reading of the majority is "nuqim" with the plural of majesty (the "we" form). Mujahid read it with the yā' of the third-person absent, meaning: Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, will not establish. Ubayd ibn Umayr read "fala yaqum" (it will not stand), which requires that he read "wazn" (weight) in the nominative. Mujahid similarly read: "So there will not stand for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight." Ubayd ibn Umayr said: On the Day of Resurrection a man, great, tall and a great eater and drinker, will be brought, and he will not weigh with Allah the wing of a gnat. I say: This cannot be said by opinion alone, and its meaning has been established as a report traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, a great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh with Allah the wing of a gnat." Recite if you wish: ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The meaning is that they have no reward, and their deeds are met with punishment, so there is no good deed for them to be weighed on the scales of the Resurrection, and whoever has no good deed is in the Fire. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: Deeds like the mountains of Tihama will be brought, and they will not weigh anything. It was also said: it may mean metaphor and figurative speech, as if He said: "So there will be no value for them with Us on that day," and Allah knows best. In this hadith there is jurisprudence (fiqh) disparaging fatness for one who strives to acquire it, because in that there is the pursuit of foods and occupation with them away from noble qualities. Rather, it indicates the prohibition of eating beyond the amount needed for sustenance, sought for luxury and fattening. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the most hateful of men to Allah, may He be exalted, is the fat scholar (habr)." And from the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The best of you is my generation, then those who follow them" – Imran said: I do not know whether he mentioned two generations after his generation or three – "then after you there will be a people who bear witness without being asked, who betray and are not trusted, who make vows and do not fulfil them, and fatness appears among them." (This is a condemnation.) The reason for this is that acquired fatness comes only from excessive eating and greed, and from ease, comfort, safety and indulgence with the self in its desires. Such a person is a slave to his self, not a slave to his Lord, and whoever is in this state inevitably falls into what is forbidden, and every flesh that grows from unlawful gain, the Fire is more fitting for it. Allah, may He be exalted, has condemned the disbelievers for their excessive eating, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ [[See vol. 16, p. 234.]] [Muhammad: 12]. So if the believer resembles them and enjoys their luxury in all his states and times, where is the reality of faith, and the performance of the duties of Islam?! Whoever eats and drinks much, his greed and eagerness increase, and his laziness and sleep increase at night, so his day is lost and his night is asleep. This meaning has passed in (al-A'raf) [[See vol. 7, p. 191 ff. and p. 165.]], and the mention of the Scale has preceded there, and that it has two pans in which the records of deeds are weighed, so there is no point in repeating it. And when they laughed at the thinness of the shin (hamsh) [[Hamsh al-saq: its thinness.]] of Ibn Mas'ud while he was climbing a palm tree, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Do you laugh at a shin that will be weighed with the deeds of the people of the earth?" This indicates that persons are weighed. This was mentioned by al-Ghaznawi.

Allah's words: ﴿That is their recompense﴾. "That" refers to the abandonment of weighing, and it is in the nominative position as a subject. "Their recompense" is its predicate, and (Hell) 106 is an apposition to the subject which is "that." The "ma" in His words "because they disbelieved" 106 is verbal (masdariyya), and "mockery" (huzu') means belittling and derision, which has been discussed.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging﴾ 107. Qatadah said: al-Firdaws is the hill of Paradise, its middle, its highest, its best and its loftiest. Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: al-Firdaws is the navel of Paradise. Ka'b said: There is no garden among the gardens higher than the Garden of al-Firdaws; in it are those who enjoin the good and forbid the evil. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes the prayer and fasts Ramadan, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise, whether he struggles in the way of Allah or sits in his land in which he was born." They said: O Messenger of Allah, should we not inform the people with glad tidings? He said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees which Allah has prepared for those who struggle in the way of Allah; between each two degrees is as between the heaven and the earth. So when you ask Allah, the Exalted, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest of Paradise – I think he said – and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth." Mujahid said: al-Firdaws is the orchard in Byzantine (Rumi) language. Al-Farra' said: it is Arabic. Al-Firdaws is a garden in Paradise. Firdaws is also the name of a meadow below al-Yamamah. Its plural is faradis. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi said:

"Their dwellings were then evident, in them the faradis, the garlic (fuwman) and the onion."

Al-Faradis is a place in Syria. And a "mufradas" vine means trellised (mu'arrash).

(Abiding therein) meaning: remaining forever.

(They will not desire to be removed from it) 108, meaning they will not seek a transfer from it to anything else. "Hiwal" means transfer (tahwil). Abu Ali said this. Al-Zajjaj said: he removed from his place "hiwalan" just as one says "he grew great in greatness" (ʿazuma ʿiẓaman). He said: It may also be from "hila" (trickery), meaning they will not seek a dwelling other than it. Al-Jawhari said: "Tahawwul" is movement from one place to another, and the noun is "hiwal," and from it is the saying of Allah: ﴿Abiding therein, they will not desire to be removed from it﴾ 108.

Allah's words: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾ 109. "Nafida" means a thing is complete and finished, and this has been discussed before.

(And even if We brought the like of it as replenishment) 109, meaning: an addition to the sea in number or weight. In the codex of Ubayy it is "midadan" 109, and so Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin and Humayd read it. "Madadan" 109 is in the accusative as a specification or as a circumstantial state (hal). Ibn Abbas said: The Jews said when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [[See vol. 10, p. 323.]] [al-Isra': 85], they said: How, when we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good? So this was revealed: "Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted" 109, to the end of the verse. It was also said: The Jews said: You have been given wisdom, and whoever has been given wisdom has been given much good; then you claim you have no knowledge of the Spirit?! So Allah, the Exalted, said: Say: even if you were given the Qur'an and you were given the Torah, it is, in relation to the words of Allah, little. Ibn Abbas said: "The words of my Lord" 109 means: the admonitions of my Lord. It was also said: By "the words" he means the eternal speech which has no limit and no end, and though it is one, it is permissible to express it with the plural form, because it contains wondrous words, and because it is a means for us through them. So the expression in plural form is permitted, for majesty. Al-A'sha said:

"And a face clear in colour, pure, adorned by it, with a neck, and with the lobes and the wrists."

The Arabic says "فَعَبَّرَ بِاللَّبَّاتِ عَنِ اللَّبَّةِ", which means he used the plural *al-labbat* to refer to the singular *al-labbah*. In the Revelation: ﴿We are your allies﴾ [Fussilat: 31][[See vol. 15, p. 357.]]. And ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder﴾ [al-Hijr: 9][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]]. And ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾ [al-Hijr: 23][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]]. Likewise ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾ [al-Nahl: 120][[See vol. 10, p. 5, p. 18 and p. 198.]], because he took the place of a nation.

It was also said: meaning, the expressions and indications that point to the understood meanings of the words of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, would not be exhausted.

Al-Suddi said: meaning, even if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the attributes of Paradise, which is the abode of reward, were exhausted.

Ikrimah said: the sea would be exhausted before the reward of the one who says "There is no god but Allah" is exhausted.

A parallel to this verse is: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman: 27][[See vol. 13, p. 76.]].

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْفَدَ" with the *ya'* (in the third person masculine), because the verb had already been mentioned.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: I know nothing except what Allah teaches me, and the knowledge of Allah, exalted be He, cannot be counted. I have only been commanded to convey to you that there is no god but Allah.

(﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110]. Meaning: whoever hopes to see Him and to receive His reward, and fears His punishment.

(﴿let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾) [al-Kahf: 110].

Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Jundub ibn Zuhayr al-'Amiri, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do an action for the sake of Allah, exalted be He, and I intend by it the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, except that when it is seen by others, it pleases me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and He does not accept what has been shared with another." Then the verse was revealed.

Tawus said: a man said, "O Messenger of Allah! I love to fight in the way of Allah, exalted be He, and I love that my position be seen," so this verse was revealed.

Mujahid said: a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah! I give charity and maintain the ties of kinship, and I do that only for Allah, exalted be He, but it is mentioned about me, and I am praised for it, and that pleases me and impresses me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent and said nothing, so Allah, exalted be He, revealed: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: all of these are meant, and the verse includes all of that and other deeds.

The sound hadith of Abu Hurairah about the three people who will be judged first among mankind has already been mentioned in Surah Hud[[See vol. 9, p. 14.]]. And the discussion of showing off (riya') has already been mentioned in Surah al-Nisa'[[See vol. 5, p. 180 onward.]], where we also mentioned from the reports there what is sufficient.

Al-Mawardi said, and all the people of interpretation said: the meaning of His saying, exalted be He: "and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110] is that he does not show off his deed to anyone.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in (Nawadir al-Usul): He said: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd told us, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, who said: I came to Shaddad ibn Aws at his place of prayer, and he was weeping. I said: "What made you weep, O Abu Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "A hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day. I saw on his face something that troubled me. I said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, what is it that I see on your face?' He said: 'A matter I fear for my community after me.' I said: 'What is it, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Shirk and hidden desire.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Will your community associate partners with Allah after you?' He said: 'O Shaddad! Indeed they will not worship the sun, nor the moon, nor a stone, nor an idol, but they will show off with their deeds.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is showing off shirk?" He said: "Yes." I said: "What is the hidden desire?" He said: "A person wakes up fasting, then the desires of this world are presented to him, and he breaks his fast." 

Abd al-Wahid said: I met al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id! Tell me about showing off: is it shirk?" He said: "Yes. Do you not recite: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord' [al-Kahf: 110]?"

Ismail ibn Ishaq narrated: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Shaddad ibn Aws were sitting together, and they said: "We fear for this community from shirk and hidden desire." As for hidden desire, it comes from women. They also said: "We heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever prays a prayer showing off with it has committed shirk, and whoever fasts a fast showing off with it has committed shirk.'" Then they recited: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110].

I say: the interpretation of hidden desire has come differently from this, and we have mentioned it in (al-Nisa')[[See vol. 5, p. 181.]].

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: al-Hasan was asked about sincerity (ikhlas) and showing off (riya'), and he said: "From sincerity is that you love to conceal your good deeds and do not love to conceal your bad deeds. If Allah makes your good deeds apparent, you say: 'This is from Your grace and kindness, and it is not from my action or my doing.'" And he recalled the saying of Allah, exalted be He: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and ﴿those who give what they give﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 60] — the verse — who give sincerity while fearing that it will not be accepted from them. As for showing off, it is seeking the portion of the self from its deed in this world. It was said to him: "How is this?" He said: "Whoever seeks, by a deed between himself and Allah, exalted be He, other than the countenance of Allah, exalted be He, and the Hereafter, that is showing off."

Our scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, said: showing off may lead its doer to be mocked by people, as it is related that Tahir ibn al-Husayn said to Abu Abd Allah al-Marwazi: "How long has it been since you came to Iraq, O Abu Abd Allah?" He said: "I entered Iraq twenty years ago, and I have been fasting for thirty years." He said: "O Abu Abd Allah, we asked you one question and you answered us with two."

Al-Asma'i related that a Bedouin prayed and lengthened his prayer, and beside him were some people. They said: "How beautiful is your prayer!" He said: "And I am fasting along with that." Compare this with the saying of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, who prayed and shortened it. It was said to him: "You have shortened it," and he said: "Indeed, it was not mixed with showing off," so he was free of their belittling by negating showing off from himself, and from the affectation in his prayer. The remedy for showing off has already been mentioned in al-Nisa', from the saying of Luqman, that it is the concealment of the deed.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated: my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told us, saying: al-Himmani informed us, saying: Jarir informed us, from Layth, from a shaykh, from [[In manuscript K: he said.]] Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Bakr said, and he testified to it upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned shirk, and he said: "It is among you more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Shall I direct you to something which, if you do it, removes from you the minor and major shirk? Say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know,' say it three times." 

Umar ibn Qays al-Kindi said: I heard Mu'awiyah recite this verse on the pulpit: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord" [al-Kahf: 110], and he said: "Indeed, it is the last verse to be revealed from the heaven."

Umar said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "It has been revealed to me that whoever recites 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds' [al-Kahf: 110], a light will be raised for him between Aden and Makkah, filled with angels who send blessings upon him and seek forgiveness for him."

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever recites the beginning of Surah al-Kahf and its end, it will be a light for him from his head to his feet, and whoever recites all of it, it will be a light for him from the earth to the sky."

It is related from Ibn Abbas that a man said to him: "I intend to get up for a while in the night, but sleep overcomes me." He said: "When you want to get up at any hour of the night you wish, recite, when you lie down on your bed: 'Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord' [al-Kahf: 109] to the end of the surah, for Allah, exalted be He, will wake you at whatever hour of the night you wish." Al-Tha'labi, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned these virtues.
